subject: dsa
title: Encode and Decode Strings
summary: Length-prefix encoding. Write each string as its length, a '#' delimiter, then its characters, so decoding reads the count and then exactly that many chars.
problem: Encode a list of strings into one string and decode it back, even when a string contains '#'.

steps.caption: Pack a list of strings into one string so it can be split back unambiguously, even if a string contains '#'. Prefix each with its length and a '#'.
Encode "ab": its length is 2, then a '#', then the chars a b. That gives the block "2#ab".
Encode "c": length 1, a '#', then c, giving "1#c". The full encoding is "2#ab1#c".
Decoding starts at index 0. It reads "2", so the next string is 2 chars long.
Skip the '#' at index 1, then read 2 chars at indices 2-3 to recover "ab".
Continue at index 4. It reads "1", so the next string is 1 char long.
Skip the '#', then read 1 char at index 6 to recover "c". Decoded back to ["ab", "c"].
